newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to take more from World Bank - Chubais.
newsitem.headline: Russia to take more from World Bank - Chubais.

text.p: Russia will take more credits from the World Bank and will cut borrowing from the International Monetary Fund, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said in a magazine interview published on Tuesday.

"We have practically reached the goals which IMF credits are aimed for. The tasks are solved and our cooperation with the IMF is nearing its completion," Chubais said in an interview in Kommersant magazine. "And with the World Bank it is vice versa. Besides a total increase of credits from the World Bank, we shall increase the volume of investment credits."

The World Bank has said it could lend Russia $3 billion a year over the next two years. Russia agreed a $10 billion three-year loan with the IMF last year, and expects to receive about $2.4 billon from it this year.
Currently the volume of the IMF credits exceeds World Bank credits five times, Chubais said.
In 1997 Russia will take $500 million in coal credit and some more money to restructure social sphere and structural reform, he said.
Chubais said Russia was in talks with the World Bank on funding the $2 billion construction of the Burei hydro-power station in the Far East.
He said Russia was able to switch to World Bank credits because of its economic stabilisation, including low inflation.
